edges.effect_quant: Across ICU studies, higher frailty consistently predicts greater mortality. A meta-analysis of 13 observational studies with 64,279 participants found frailty associated with increased short-term mortality (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.45 to 1.98) and in-hospital mortality (RR 1.73, 95% CI 1.55 to 1.93). In a geriatric ICU cohort using a deficit-accumulation frailty index, each 1% increase in the index was associated with an 11% increase in 30-day mortality risk.
edges.population: older adults admitted to intensive care units, especially patients aged 65 years or older evaluated for frailty before or at ICU admission
edges.mechanism: A higher frailty index represents multisystem deficit accumulation and reduced physiologic reserve. Under the stress of critical illness, frail patients are less able to tolerate organ dysfunction, invasive support, and prolonged recovery, making early mortality more likely.
edges.summary: This is a strong harmful prognostic edge. Whether measured directly with a frailty index or pooled across closely related frailty tools, baseline frailty in older ICU patients consistently identifies a group with substantially higher short-term mortality and poorer downstream outcomes.
edges.caveats: Not every ICU study uses the exact same frailty instrument, so the pooled literature blends deficit-accumulation indices with other validated frailty measures. That means the edge is best interpreted as support for frailty-index-like vulnerability as a mortality predictor, rather than as a claim about one single scoring format only.

evidence.notes: Association of Frailty With the Risk of Mortality and Resource Utilization in Elderly Patients in Intensive Care Units: A Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: short-term mortality in frail versus non-frail older adults admitted to intensive care units

evidence.citation: ZengA et al 2015 J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci
evidence.notes: Mortality in Relation to Frailty in Patients Admitted to a Specialized Geriatric Intensive Care Unit.

effect_quant.comparator: increase in 30-day mortality risk for each 1% increase in frailty index at ICU admission

evidence.citation: LauneyY et al 2019 Ann Intensive Care
evidence.notes: Risk factors of frailty and death or only frailty after intensive care in non-frail elderly patients: a prospective non-interventional study.
